methodology.summary: Reusing an item avoids the emissions of making a new one. We estimate that from the item's weight and main material, subtract the emissions of moving it there and back, and give a range: an upper bound and a conservative bound.

formula.upper: weight (t) x quantity x material factor (kgCO2e/t) - transport
formula.conservative: weight (t) x quantity x material factor / 10 uses - transport
formula.transport: transport factor (kgCO2e/t-km) x weight (t) x quantity x distance (km) x 2 legs

assumptions.note: ASSUMPTION, not sourced: a new item bought for this event would serve 10 events in its life. No citable figure was found for event-equipment reuse cycles (checked 14 Nov 2026: only vendor lifespan claims in years). Change it here; every result recomputes.
Modelling choice: delivery to the event plus return to the supplier (the empty truck's return is not counted). The per tonne-km factor itself is sourced.
Each item's weight and main material are rough estimates for fictional demo data.

status_labels.sourced: Every input is from a published source (no demo estimates).
status_labels.illustrative: At least one input is an estimate or an assumption: show as an estimate, never as a verified claim.
status_labels.unavailable: Weight, material or factor missing: no number is shown.

not_counted: Delivery of the new item that was not bought
Empty truck runs: only the two loaded legs (delivery, then return of the items) are counted
limitations: UK factors are used as a proxy for Turkey.
Material factors are per tonne of material, not per finished product; manufacturing and packaging are not modelled separately.
The conservative bound depends on an assumed number of uses with no citable source.
All inventory in this prototype is fictional.
